text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police forces caught a suspect who is charged with killing two policemen last August.

- Opposition parties offer Albanian homes as accommodation for observers to the October 20 local elections who cannot secure hotel rooms. The ruling party members in the central electoral commission said the lack of hotel space did not allow more than 200 international observers to come to Albania for the polls.
- The United States will send less than 100 observers for the October 20 local elections, but many others will be invited by a U.S. non-governmental organisation.

- The Central Electoral Commission has begun considering the participation of President Sali Berisha in the electoral campaign for his ruling Democratic Party. The opposition says his involvement in the campaign was unconstitutional.

- The Council of Europe will suspend Albania from the forum if a round-table of the parties does not function properly, said two opposition leaders back from Strasbourg. The Council considers the local elections to be an important test of Albania's young democracy.
- Independent Trade Union to meet the government again on compensation from recent price rises. It has already announced a one-day strike for October 4.
- Value-added tax, in effect since July 1, has significantly increased revenues for the government.
- Albania beat Macedonia 1-0 in an under-21 soccer friendly.
- A baby was born with the AIDS virus after the mother received a blood transfusion during pregnancy.
- Some 30 European MPs will monitor Albania's local elections. The Council of Europe will head international observation.
- The government decided against imposing VAT on gas used for heating and cooking.
- President Sali Berisha hosted a reception for the contestants of Miss Europe 96.
- Socialist Party complains the Finance Ministry has not yet delivered the money it needs for the electoral campaign.
